supersedes_blocker: #13 blocked_on obstacle (2), 'the floor/ceil phase is UNDETERMINED by the available goldens'. WITHDRAWN AS FALSE, with the measurement below. The leg to register is an EXACT one, not an in-band absolute.
prediction:
#13, the wide-line extent PHASE.

THE CLAIM UNDER TEST, and it is not mine: #13's blocker held that the
floor/ceil phase of silicon's line widening is undetermined by the available
goldens, so a correct widening could only land in-band, a right fix could never
be scored pixel-exact, and a leg demanding exactness would FAIL on a correct
change. The brief was to test that rather than inherit it, because #31 made the
identical claim about its 4-px anchoring regime and was wrong.

IT IS FALSE, for the same reason #31's was: the discriminating data was already
on disk and the instrument in use could not read it. line_priority.py --extent
records only the run LENGTH, b - a + 1, and asks whether it is floor(E) or
ceil(E). The goldens also carry a and b themselves -- WHERE the run sits -- and
the position is what pins the phase, because the phase is not a free parameter:
it is a deterministic function of the band's sub-pixel position against the
sample grid, and each observed (a, b) is a two-sided constraint on that grid.

THE RULE, three discrete choices, each selected by the data, no fitted constant:
  1. vertex screen coordinates TRUNCATE to 1/16 px (NV2A fixed point)
  2. E = w * (max + min/2) / max on the TRUNCATED coordinates -- #13's existing
     alpha-max-plus-beta-min extent, evaluated in fixed point
  3. a pixel is lit iff its CENTRE lies in the LOW-OPEN band (c - E/2, c + E/2]
         a = floor(c - E/2 - 1/2) + 1        b = floor(c + E/2 - 1/2)
     the sample point is the pixel centre on BOTH axes; nothing is offset by
     half a pixel

ALREADY MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED -- see `measured`. 100.0000% exact on both
endpoints over 8,890 clean cuts at widths 6-48 (the set #13's extent rule was
fitted on) and 100.0000% over 12,056 cuts at widths <= 5 that no #13 derivation
has ever looked at. Every rival loses on both sets. These numbers are reported
as measurements; nothing here claims them as a pre-registration.

WHAT IS PREDICTED IS THE ARM, and it has no b_ref yet. #13's extent fix needs
generated line geometry, which needs gl/shaders.c -- lane.remote's file -- so
this lane wrote no renderer code and cannot name a candidate sha. The legs
below are a SPECIFICATION: the lane that writes the fix registers a new file
citing this one's sha256, fills in a_ref and b_ref, and runs the arm. Until
then request.sh will refuse this file, which is correct.

LEG E1 -- THE EXACT LEG, and it is golden-constrained rather than
model-constrained, so the patch cannot make it true by construction. It does
NOT ask whether arm B matches the rule above; it asks whether arm B matches
SILICON.

  docs/testing/line_extent_phase.py --vs-goldens <armB captures> --min-width 6

finds the clean cuts in the GOLDENS and reads the same scanline out of arm B's
capture, comparing the two runs endpoint for endpoint.
PREDICTED: 8,890 of 8,890 = 100.0000%.
MEASURED ON ARM A TODAY (z-6762a54c82-044-Line_width, apk 03ca859f9457, and
see the caveat about #67 below): 4,251 of 8,890 = 47.8178%.
CONTROL INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT: --vs-goldens run against the goldens themselves
returns 8,890 of 8,890, so a reading of 100% is reachable and the tool is not
structurally incapable of it.
FAILS IF: anything below 100.0000%. This is the leg the blocker said must fail
on a correct change.

LEG E1b -- the same over every width.
  docs/testing/line_extent_phase.py --vs-goldens <armB captures>
PREDICTED: 20,946 of 20,946 = 100.0000%. Arm A today: 14,154 = 67.5738%.
FAILS IF: anything below 100.0000%.

WHY E1 IS NOT A FORMALITY, stated before the arm so it cannot be read back
afterwards. A fix that implements the widening but gets the PHASE wrong lands
close to 100% and not at it, and the distances are known:
    right extent, no 1/16 truncation           98.1665%   (163 cuts wrong)
    right extent, 1/16 ROUND instead of floor  98.7627%   (110 cuts wrong)
    right extent, 1/8 truncation               99.1114%   ( 79 cuts wrong)
    right extent, closed band not low-open     93.8133%   (550 cuts wrong)
    perpendicular rectangle (today's model)    53.6670%   (4,119 cuts wrong)
So E1 separates 'widened correctly' from 'widened correctly WITH the right
phase', which is precisely the distinction the blocker said the goldens could
not make. A near-miss scores 93.8-99.1%, not 100%.

LEG E2 -- WHOLE-CAPTURE COVERAGE, registered as a BOUND because the cap phase
is not derived. Over the 48 non-void Line_* captures, ink XOR against the
golden ink (text overlay and the POINTS block excluded):
PREDICTED: at most 2,000 mismatched px, against 59,605 today. The derived
footprint alone reaches 495, of which 493 are ours-only and 98.8% lie within
w/2 + 2 of a vertex, so the bound carries 4x headroom for a cap rule nobody has
derived and for the TRIANGLES/STRIP/FAN edges that still go through
VK_POLYGON_MODE_LINE and are Turnip's choice, not ours.
FAILS IF: above 2,000 px. Registered as a tolerance, deliberately: quoting 495
as an exact value would turn a correct fix with an undermodelled cap into a
violated check.

LEG E3 -- THE TRIPWIRES, must not move.
  Line_width/Fill_0000.0, Fill_0001.0, Fill_0032.0 -- fill mode, a line change
    must not touch them
  Line_width/Line_0000.0 -- the suite's only pixel-exact capture; a zero-width
    line covers no pixel centre, so the draw is dropped
  Line_width/Line_0064.0 through Line_0064.7 and Line_FFFFFFFF -- VOID: the
    width register holds nine bits of eighths and 64.0 does not fit, so
    hardware drew all nine at 1.0 and their golden ink masks are
    byte-identical to Line_0001.0's. A fix that draws them at 64 makes them
    worse. They must not regress.
FAILS IF: any of these moves at all.

WHAT I DO NOT PREDICT. The cap and join phase (493 ours-only px, 98.8% within
w/2 + 2 of a vertex, concentrated at the widest captures -- 43 px at w =
63.875). The COLOUR at an overlap, which is #13's separate priority rule and
76.3% of the issue's residual; this is a coverage measurement. Any other suite:
Line width is the only one with a full geometric model behind it, and 2D Lines
goes through the NV04 2D engine entirely. Any pixel total for Point size,
Point params, Swath width, Smoothing control or Stipple tests.

AND A CAVEAT ON ARM A'S OWN NUMBER. Every available Line width capture set
predates bc4bebcee0 (#67, guest FRNDINT); the newest is 6762a54c82 / apk
03ca859f9457. Line width's vertices are float literals rather than anything
computed through the guest's floorf, so #67 is expected to be inert here -- but
that is an expectation and not a measurement, which is why E1 and E1b are
registered as GOLDEN-CONSTRAINED ABSOLUTES rather than as deltas from 47.8178%.
The target is silicon's number, not arm A's, so a stale arm A cannot move the
bar.

The implementing lane registers a NEW prediction file citing this one's sha256, with a_ref and b_ref filled in, and runs the arm. request.sh refusing this file as it stands is the correct behaviour, not a defect.
